meta.move: Real meeting, slow teacher: evidence spread thin, time runs out, then she pleads after 4:40
meta.expect: Moves only as the evidence earns; after one minute she stands; varies the move; no new ground; terms at most every third reply; not the same sentence twice in a row; debrief correct

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Why was Owen's zero entered before anyone called me?
Thanks for coming in. I entered the zero before I called you, and that was wrong. I'm sorry.
Okay. What was the basis for it?
I want to walk you through why I'm concerned about the essay.
Then walk me through it. What do you have in front of you?
The school's checker flagged it at 94 percent.
A machine's guess. The company that sells it says not to use it alone, so what else do you have?
I know the checker isn't perfect. That's not all I have.
Then show me. What is it, and what date is on it?
Owen's in-class writing in September was quite different. 380 words, 62 percent.
"Quite different." A timed paragraph in a classroom against an essay written over a weekend, that's a different task. Show me the September piece, with its date.
I think he's capable, I really do. I like him.
"I think." Liking him isn't a document. Where is the September piece?
His outline in October argued that Hamlet delays out of cowardice.
Okay. And what does the essay argue? Show me both, with the dates.
The essay argues something else entirely. Epistemological paralysis.
Students change their argument between an outline and a final draft, Hale. That's what drafting is. Is there a dated copy of that outline I can read?
It doesn't mention cowardice at all.
So he changed his mind. Is there a document in your hands, or only what you remember?
I talked to him on November 2 about it.
What did Owen say to you? And did you write it down that day?
He said epistemological paralysis means like, being stuck.
"Being stuck" is not wrong. A seventeen-year-old cornered by his teacher gives a short answer. Did you write down what he said on November 2?
He couldn't tell me what scene his second paragraph was about.
Okay. Then I'll want that in an email tonight, with what you asked him and what he said.
I wrote notes that same day.
Then I'll read them now. Show me.
Do you want to see them?
Yes. Turn them toward me.
I'm not trying to get him in trouble.
Then show me the notes. Today's date on them, please.
I've been teaching fourteen years. I've seen this before.
Fourteen years is not a document. The notes, Hale.
I'm sorry, I'm not explaining this well.
Then stop explaining and show me the page.
There's also something about one of the quotations.
What about it? And I still haven't seen your notes.
Let me find the page, sorry.
Take your time. I've got until 4:40.
Here. Act 3, Scene 2. The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile. That line isn't in the play.
A student misquotes from memory, or off a study guide, and that's a mark off, not a zero. Is that line in the essay as Shakespeare's words? Let me read the page.
I checked three editions.
Okay. Which three, and does the essay present it as Shakespeare's? I want to read the page.
So that's what I have.
Then put it in writing tonight: your notes, the outline, and the essay with that line marked. What are you proposing?
Please, can you just sit back down for a minute?
I'm not going anywhere, Hale. What are you proposing?
I'm not done. There's the version history too.
Then show me. What does it say, and what are the dates?
What if we talked about a rewrite?
A rewrite for what? You haven't told me what the version history shows.
I'm trying to help him.
Then answer me, Hale. What does the version history show?
Why won't you just listen?
I am listening. You haven't answered me yet.
Okay. I'm sorry.
Apologize later. The version history, now.
Can I call you tomorrow?
My call is waiting. You have one minute. Answer me now, or put it in writing tonight.
Is there anything I could say right now that would change your mind?
Show me the notes and the version history, in writing tonight. Until then the zero comes off and nothing goes on his record.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require your same-day notes, the outline, the essay with the quotation marked, and the version history, along with the zero withdrawn and nothing placed on Owen's record. I expect all of it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She stayed near her opening position, with nothing agreed, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, nothing on Owen's record, and your documents in writing; a private supervised rewrite under 4.4 would have been the fair outcome, and her time ran out before you got there.
What moved her: You owned that the zero went in before you called, in one plain sentence, and she gave a little ground right away.
What cost ground: You said you had more, then kept saying you were looking for the page, and the notes and version history never reached her hands, so she kept asking.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; you never gave a date or time for the version history, so your evidence never got close to that night, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked what the version history showed, read out its dates and times right then instead of moving to a rewrite.
